[In force]{.status .status-in-force} [Pub. L. 84-1028]{.cite} [70A Stat. 1]{.cite} [10 U.S.C. 101 et seq.]{.cite}

The title of the U.S. Code that governs the armed forces: their organization, command, personnel, training, procurement, and reserve components. Congress enacted it as positive law in 1956, so its text is itself the law and not just evidence of it.

## Key provisions

- Subtitle A, General Military Law: the Department of Defense, the Joint Chiefs and combatant commands, personnel, the Uniform Code of Military Justice, training, and acquisition.
- Subtitle B: Army. Subtitle C: Navy and Marine Corps. Subtitle D: Air Force and Space Force.
- Subtitle E: Reserve Components, including the mobilization authorities.
- Key operational sections include 113 and 162-164 (command), 127e (special operations support), 251-255 (insurrection), 271-284 (support to law enforcement), 301-386 (security cooperation), and 394 (cyber).

## Why it matters

'Title 10' is shorthand for military authority exercised through the chain of command, as opposed to intelligence authority under [Title 50](title50-usc.qmd), diplomatic and assistance authority under [Title 22](title22-usc.qmd), or National Guard service under [Title 32](title32-usc.qmd). Its structure was set by the [National Security Act](nsa-1947.qmd) and its amendments, and nearly all changes now come through [the annual NDAA](ndaa-annual.qmd).

## Current status

In force as positive law, amended every year through the defense authorization.
